names.name: Brahman, unthinkable and unmanifest, without and with qualities (Sūrya Siddhānta 1.1)
Vāsudeva, the supreme Brahman; Aniruddha as the Sun-Hiraṇyagarbha (SS 12.12–21)
Ka — one and many, the true deity, the supreme Brahman (Āryabhaṭīya 1.1)
Viṣṇu, one and unmanifest, with the powers Śrī, Bhū and Nīlā; Janārdana in the form of the planets (BPHS 1.9–20; 2.3)
The Sun as self of all embodied beings, self of Kālapuruṣa, maker of time and door of liberation (Yogayātrā 1.1; BJ 1.1; 2.1)
Kāla, time — the destroyer of worlds (SS 1.10)

descriptions: acintya-avyakta-rūpa, nirguṇa yet guṇātman, support of the world (SS 1.1)
one quarter manifest, three quarters immortal (SS 12.20; BPHS 1.10–11)
present in all beings as the supreme-Self portion beside the jīva-portion (BPHS 1.21–24)
gives beings the fruits of karma in the form of the planets (BPHS 2.3)
relation_to_self: The Sun is the self of Kālapuruṣa and of all embodied beings (BJ 2.1; Yogayātrā 1.1); each being has a portion of the individual soul and a portion of the supreme Self (BPHS 1.21–24); the ātmakāraka signifies the self in the chart.
relation_to_world: The Lord divides himself into the twelve signs and twenty-seven asterisms (SS 12.25); time is his form; the planets are his forms and avatāras dispensing karma (BPHS 2.3–7); the earth-globe stands in space by Brahman's supporting power (SS 12.32).
caveat: Jyotiṣa is a limb (aṅga) of the Veda — its eye — and a science of time and of the ripening of karma, not itself a soteriology. It names the ultimate only in invocations and in cosmogonies borrowed from Pāñcarātra, Purāṇic and Vedāntic frames, and different texts invoke different ultimates (Brahman, Vāsudeva, Viṣṇu, the Sun, Ka); it would not claim that reading or remedying the chart liberates, though horā names the configurations that indicate liberation (BJ 25.15; Jaimini 1.2.69). A one-truth reading should not be read back into it as its own doctrine.
